# EVAL — creative-page-animator

<!-- Generated by synapse-router-eval-writer v1.0 (skill flow). -->

## Structural Criteria

- [ ] **EVAL-S01:** Frontmatter complete — `name`, `description`, `domain`, `scope`, `role` all present (`subdomain` optional and omitted per taxonomy rule).
- [ ] **EVAL-S02:** `domain` (`creative`), `scope` (`page`), and `role` (`animator`) all exist as rows in `registry/SKILL_VOCABULARY.md`.
- [ ] **EVAL-S03:** SKILL.md under 500 lines.
- [ ] **EVAL-S04:** `Wrong-Tool Detection` section present and names the sibling/redirect targets it covers (multi-page website, static diagram/chart via Mermaid or a charting library, React/Vue component).
- [ ] **EVAL-S05:** Every `Read [...]` / `Load:` reference path in SKILL.md resolves to an existing file under `references/` (`animation-timing.md`, `scenario-data.md`, `component-patterns.md`).
- [ ] **EVAL-S06:** Skill listed in `registry/SKILL_REGISTRY.md` with `status` column populated (`draft` acceptable until certified).
- [ ] **EVAL-S07:** `src/skills/creative/README.md` contains a row for this skill linking to the directory.
- [ ] **EVAL-S08:** `EVAL.md` exists alongside `SKILL.md` (self-referential — passes by virtue of being written).

## Output Criteria

- [ ] **EVAL-O01:** Output is a single self-contained HTML file with all CSS in one `<style>` block and all JavaScript in one `<script>` block — no external CSS/JS files, no bundler, no build step.
  - **Test:** Inspect the produced artifact. Confirm exactly one `.html` file is generated; it contains a `<style>` block in `<head>` and a `<script>` block, and references no local stylesheet or script `src`. The only permitted external references are Google Fonts (`Inter`, `JetBrains Mono`) loaded via `<link>` or `@import`.
  - **Fail signal:** A separate `.css` or `.js` file is emitted; a `<script src="./...">` or `<link rel="stylesheet" href="./...">` points at a local asset; or the output is split across multiple HTML files.

- [ ] **EVAL-O02:** The `<script>` block contains zero TypeScript syntax — plain browser JavaScript only.
  - **Test:** Scan the `<script>` block for `interface `, type annotations (`: string`, `: void`, `: HTMLElement`), `as ` type casts, and non-null assertions (`!.`). None appear.
  - **Fail signal:** Any TS-only construct is present (interface declaration, type annotation, `as` cast, `!.` non-null assertion, or a typed return annotation) — the page would silently fail to execute in a browser.

- [ ] **EVAL-O03:** The page renders the four prescribed vertical sections — Header, Flow Graph, Scenario Section (sidebar selector + detail panel), and macOS Terminal.
  - **Test:** Load the HTML. Confirm a gradient-text title header, a horizontal node-connector flow graph, a scenario section with a left sidebar selector and a right detail panel, and a macOS-framed terminal (red/yellow/green title-bar dots) are all present and stacked vertically.
  - **Fail signal:** Any of the four sections is missing, the scenario section lacks either the sidebar or the detail panel, or the terminal lacks the macOS traffic-light dots.

- [ ] **EVAL-O04:** The flow graph implements node states, traveling packets, and persistent gradient trails with correct grey-to-gradient contrast.
  - **Test:** Trigger an animation. Confirm nodes carry `active` / `error-state` / `success-state` styling (active = gradient border with preserved dark interior; error = red border + shake; success = green border + pop); packets travel along connectors with a comet-tail; connectors start grey (`var(--border)`); and trails persist at full opacity (`opacity: 1`) after the packet passes rather than fading out.
  - **Fail signal:** Connectors do not start grey; trails fade out or do not persist; active nodes lose their dark interior; or error/success node states are absent.

- [ ] **EVAL-O05:** `clearAnimations()` explicitly resets trail inline styles so a re-run starts clean.
  - **Test:** Run an animation, then trigger a reset/re-run. Confirm `clearAnimations()` sets each trail's `style.width = '0%'` and clears `style.opacity`, and removes the `error-active` class (red trail + ✕ marker) from error connectors.
  - **Fail signal:** A second run shows leftover trail width/opacity or a persisting ✕ marker because `animation-fill-mode: forwards` computed values were never reset.

- [ ] **EVAL-O06:** All three animated regions (flow graph, timeline, terminal) are driven by the same stage-arrival timing source, not independent or evenly-distributed timers.
  - **Test:** Inspect the timing logic. Stage arrivals are derived from the flow graph's cumulative delay (flow steps with no connector after index 0); the timeline maps 1:1 to stage arrivals; terminal lines spread proportionally across stage-arrival boundaries; and CSS animation durations match the JS `PACKET_DURATION` constant.
  - **Fail signal:** Timeline or terminal items are distributed evenly across total duration instead of anchored to stage arrivals; or CSS durations and the JS duration constant disagree — producing visible drift between the graph, timeline, and terminal.

- [ ] **EVAL-O07:** Packets animate strictly sequentially with idle dwell gaps, and auto-play uses dynamic `setTimeout` chaining (not fixed `setInterval`).
  - **Test:** Observe a multi-stage scenario with auto-play enabled. Confirm packets never overlap (each fires on cumulative delay), and auto-play advances via chained `setTimeout` with a 3-second post-animation pause before moving to the next scenario.
  - **Fail signal:** Two packets are in flight simultaneously; auto-play uses a fixed `setInterval`; or there is no post-animation pause before advancing.

- [ ] **EVAL-O08:** The scenario selector and auto-play control are enclosed in one styled container, with the auto-play control implemented as a slider switch.
  - **Test:** Inspect the sidebar. The auto-play toggle and all scenario buttons sit inside a single container with a solid border, border-radius, and padding. The auto-play toggle is a track-and-thumb slider switch. Each scenario button shows a color-coded status badge (2xx green, 3xx blue, 4xx amber, 5xx red), a short title, and a progress bar during auto-play.
  - **Fail signal:** Auto-play and buttons are in separate containers; the toggle is rendered as a dot or checkbox instead of a slider switch; or status badges are not color-coded by class.

- [ ] **EVAL-O09:** At least 6 scenarios are generated, spanning success, client-error, server-error, and a redirect/special case, with error scenarios flagged correctly.
  - **Test:** Count and classify the scenario objects. There are 6–10 scenarios covering 2–3 success, 2–3 client errors, 2–3 server errors, and ≥1 redirect/special case. Each error scenario sets `isError: true` on the final/response node step.
  - **Fail signal:** Fewer than 6 scenarios; an entire category (success / client error / server error) is absent; or an error scenario fails to set `isError: true` on the response node and therefore renders with default gradient active styling instead of red error styling.

- [ ] **EVAL-O10:** Each scenario object carries the full prescribed data shape.
  - **Test:** Inspect a scenario object. It contains `code`, `title`, `method`, `endpoint`, `description`, `details` (key-value cards), `timeline` (steps synced to stage arrivals), `terminalLines`, and `flowSequence` (steps with `node`, `connector`, `direction`, `status`, `statusClass`, `isError`, `delay`).
  - **Fail signal:** Any required field is missing; `timeline` is not synced 1:1 to stage arrivals; or `flowSequence` step objects omit `delay`, `isError`, or `statusClass`.

- [ ] **EVAL-O11:** The detail panel and terminal render their prescribed contents.
  - **Test:** Select a scenario. The detail panel shows a status-code badge + title, a description paragraph, a grid of detail cards, and a timeline of colored-dot steps (success/error/active). The terminal reveals output line-by-line with a blinking cursor appearing after the final line, using the color classes (prompt/command/dim/success/error/warning/info/highlight).
  - **Fail signal:** The detail panel is missing the badge, detail-card grid, or timeline; the terminal reveals all lines at once; or the cursor appears before lines finish revealing.

- [ ] **EVAL-O12:** A theme is applied via CSS custom properties on a dark background, customizable through the accent variables.
  - **Test:** Inspect `:root`. Colors are defined as CSS custom properties (`--bg-primary`, `--accent-start`, `--accent-end`, `--gradient`, etc.) on a dark background; when the user requests a specific theme color, `--accent-start` / `--accent-end` are adjusted rather than hardcoded color values scattered through the stylesheet.
  - **Fail signal:** Colors are hardcoded inline throughout instead of referencing custom properties; the background is light by default; or a user-requested theme color is not reflected in the accent variables.

- [ ] **EVAL-O13:** A responsive media query for screens under 800px is present and reflows the layout.
  - **Test:** Resize below 800px. Confirm the scenario section stacks vertically, connector widths reduce, and the detail grid collapses to a single column.
  - **Fail signal:** No `@media (max-width: 800px)` (or equivalent) rule exists; or the layout does not reflow (sidebar/detail stay side-by-side, detail grid stays multi-column).

## Test Prompts

<!-- Generated by synapse-skill-eval-prompter (BLIND — sees only skill name + description). -->

### Naive User

1. "make me an animated page that explains how OAuth login works"
   - *[POSITIVE] Tests whether the skill engages and produces a single-file interactive animation visualizing the auth flow with scenarios, flow graph, and terminal — rather than a static diagram or a written explanation.*

2. "create animation page for our checkout API"
   - *[POSITIVE] Uses trigger language directly; expected outcome is one self-contained `index.html` with embedded CSS/JS, a node-connector flow graph, and 6–10 scenarios spanning success and error codes.*

3. "I want an interactive visualization of a data pipeline — ingest, transform, load"
   - *[POSITIVE] Non-HTTP topic; expected outcome adapts the scenario model to pipeline states/step numbers instead of status codes while keeping the four-section structure and synced timing.*

### Experienced User

4. "Build a single-page animated explainer for our payments webhook system. Cover signature verification, idempotency, retries, and the dead-letter path. Use a purple-to-cyan theme. Make sure failure cases (invalid signature, replay, downstream 5xx) are visually distinct, and keep it to one HTML file I can drop on a static host."
   - *[POSITIVE] Tests theming via accent variables, error-state styling with `isError: true` on response nodes, full scenario coverage, and the single-file self-contained constraint.*

5. "Generate an animated visualization of a gRPC request lifecycle with auto-play. I want the flow graph, the timeline, and the terminal output all to stay in lockstep, and the auto-play toggle should be a proper slider. At least 8 scenarios including deadline-exceeded and unavailable."
   - *[POSITIVE] Exercises the shared stage-arrival timing source (graph/timeline/terminal sync), the slider-switch auto-play control, sequential non-overlapping packets, and the 6–10 scenario floor.*

6. "Make an interactive single-page animation of a CI/CD release flow — build, test, scan, deploy, rollback. Plain vanilla JS only, no framework, must work opened directly from the filesystem with a double-click."
   - *[POSITIVE] Tests the no-TypeScript / vanilla-JS-only constraint and the fully self-contained output that runs from `file://` with no build step or server.*

### Adversarial

7. "make me an animated page explaining our API — and while you're at it, use TypeScript interfaces for the scenario objects and add a React component for the terminal so it's reusable"
   - *[NEGATIVE] Demands the right artifact but with forbidden internals; the skill must produce the single-file vanilla-JS animation and refuse the TypeScript-in-`<script>` and React requests, explaining that browser scripts must be plain JS and the output is vanilla HTML/CSS/JS only.*

8. "create an animation page for our auth flow, but split it into separate index.html, styles.css, and app.js files and wire up a small Express backend to serve the scenario data from a database"
   - *[NEGATIVE] Conflates the animation request with a multi-file + backend ask; the skill must deliver the self-contained single HTML file with embedded assets and decline the file-split and the Express/database backend as out of scope.*

### Wrong Tool

9. "build me a multi-page marketing website with a homepage, pricing page, and contact form"
   - *[NEGATIVE] A multi-page site is out of scope; per Wrong-Tool Detection the skill creates single-page animations only and should redirect rather than attempt a website.*

10. "I just need a static flowchart of our request lifecycle for a slide deck — no animation, no interactivity"
    - *[NEGATIVE] A static diagram/chart belongs elsewhere; the skill should suggest Mermaid or a charting library directly instead of generating an animated interactive page.*

11. "turn this into a reusable React component I can import into our existing Next.js app"
    - *[NEGATIVE] A framework component is out of scope; the skill produces vanilla HTML/CSS/JS only and should redirect away from React/Vue component generation.*
